question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European Maritime Strategies and their Key Pioneers/Advocates]
options: Blue Water Policy — Francisco de Almeida (Portuguese)
Policy of Imperial Fortresses/Cartaz — Afonso de Albuquerque (Portuguese)
Monopoly and Territorial Colonization in Indonesia — Jan Pieterszoon Coen (Dutch)
League of Armed Neutrality — Robert Clive (English)
wrong_fact: The League of Armed Neutrality (1780) was pioneered by Empress Catherine the Great of Russia to protect neutral shipping from the British Royal Navy's aggressive search tactics during the American Revolutionary War, NOT by Robert Clive.
explanation: Francisco de Almeida advocated the 'Blue Water Policy' (limiting land conquests and focusing on naval dominance). Afonso de Albuquerque established a network of fortresses at strategic choke points combined with the Cartaz system. Jan Pieterszoon Coen laid the foundation of Dutch monopoly and territorial rule from Batavia. The League of Armed Neutrality was a European coalition led by Russia to resist British maritime hegemony, completely unrelated to Robert Clive.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Strategic Bases and their Intended Maritime Purpose]
options: Batavia (Jakarta) — Central Dutch administrative and trade hub connecting the Indian Ocean and East Asia
Bombay (Mumbai) — Portuguese naval shipyard gifted to the English to counter Maratha naval raids
Trincomalee (Ceylon) — Deep-water harbor coveted by English and French to control the Bay of Bengal during monsoons
St. Helena — South Atlantic island station used as a provisioning stop for return voyages to Europe
wrong_fact: Bombay was gifted to the English (Charles II) in 1661 as part of the royal dowry of Catherine of Braganza, NOT as a shipyard specifically gifted to counter Maratha naval raids, which only became a major threat decades later under Kanhoji Angre.
explanation: Batavia served as the heart of the Dutch maritime empire. Trincomalee in Ceylon was highly prized because its natural harbor offered shelter and strategic control of the Bay of Bengal during the northeast and southwest monsoons. St. Helena was a vital English East India Company outpost in the Atlantic for ships returning from India. Bombay was transferred to the English through a royal marriage treaty (dowry) in 1661, not as a tactical gift to counter Marathas.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Maritime Treaties/Concepts and their Geographic Scope/Context]
options: Treaty of Tordesillas (1494) — Meridian line 370 leagues west of Cape Verde dividing non-Christian lands between Spain and Portugal
Treaty of Zaragoza (1529) — Anti-meridian line in the Pacific determining the boundary of Spanish and Portuguese influence in the Spice Islands
Mare Liberum (1609) — Hugo Grotius's legal treatise advocating free navigation of the oceans, specifically targeting Portuguese monopoly in the Baltic Sea
Treaty of Westminster (1674) — Solidified Dutch and English spheres of influence, confirming English control of New York and Dutch dominance in Surinam
wrong_fact: Mare Liberum was written by Hugo Grotius to contest the Portuguese monopoly over the East Indies (Indian Ocean and Southeast Asia trade), NOT the Baltic Sea.
explanation: Grotius wrote Mare Liberum ('The Free Sea') on behalf of the Dutch East India Company to justify the Dutch seizure of the Portuguese carrack Santa Catarina in the Strait of Malacca and to argue that the oceans were international territory open to trade. The Treaty of Tordesillas (Atlantic/Americas partition), Treaty of Zaragoza (Pacific/Moluccas partition), and Treaty of Westminster (Anglo-Dutch peace) are all correctly matched.
